articles.title: 94 civilians killed in Mali drone strikes by army, Russian forces: Report
articles.summary: Mali's armed forces and their Russian allies have carried out what human rights watch (HRW) described as “apparent indiscriminate” drone strikes, along
articles.body: Mali's armed forces and their Russian allies have carried out what human rights watch (HRW) described as “apparent indiscriminate” drone strikes, along with other abuses, during an intensified offensive against insurgents in recent months. The operations have killed dozens of civilians, the rights group said in a report released on Monday.According to the report, drone strikes and the resulting civilian deaths more than doubled between April and August compared with the same period last year, citing data from the armed conflict location and event data project (ACLED). The escalation came in response to nationwide attacks by the regional al-Qaeda affiliate Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) and Tuareg-led separatists.The insurgent offensive, launched on April 25, killed Mali's defence minister and targeted several towns and cities, as well as the main airport in the capital, Bamako. The attacks highlighted the government's continuing struggle to restore security in the landlocked west african nation, according to the Reuters.Military leaders, who seized power in coups in 2020 and 2021 have increasingly relied on Russia to support their campaign against insurgent groups. Following the April attacks, they also deployed the Russian paramilitary group Africa Corps as part of their response.Data from the US-based conflict monitor ACLED showed that Malian forces and africa Corps conducted 47 drone strikes that killed 94 civilians between April and August. During the corresponding period a year earlier, 22 strikes had resulted in 44 civilian deaths.Strikes hit cattle market, health centreHuman Rights Watch documented several incidents it described as apparent indiscriminate drone strikes. These included an August 19 attack on a cattle market in the Bandiagara region of central Mali that killed six men.The report also cited a pre-dawn drone strike on July 29 targeting a health centre in the northern Kidal region, near the Algerian border.In addition to drone attacks, the rights group recorded other alleged abuses by Malian forces. In one incident on July 12 in the Segou region, soldiers allegedly shot and killed five young girls after mistaking them for attackers, according to the report.A spokesperson for the Malian army did not respond to a request for comment. Human rights watch said it had also received no response to a letter sent on August 5 to Mali's new defence minister outlining its findings.Mali has previously denied killing civilians during counterinsurgency operations. The Russian embassy in Bamako did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Africa Corps' involvement.Insurgent groups also accused of abusesThe Human rights watch report also documented alleged abuses by JNIM and the Tuareg-led separatists, including the execution of 19 soldiers in the northern Gao region in July.JNIM's sharia committee acknowledged to the rights group that the killings had taken place but denied ordering them. It also said such acts were not part of its policy.The Tuareg-led azawad liberation front denied executing the soldiers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2007, a couple gave $1.5 million to revive UNLV's dead debate programme; 11 years later, it was ranked No. 5 in America
articles.summary: In 2007, a $1.5 million donation from Sanford and Sandra Berman helped bring the University of Nevada, Las Vegas (UNLV) debate programme back to life
articles.body: In 2007, a $1.5 million donation from Sanford and Sandra Berman helped bring the University of Nevada, Las Vegas (UNLV) debate programme back to life after nearly a decade without a team. What followed was a remarkable rise in competitive university debating, driven by dedicated students, coaching and a growing record of tournament victories. By March 2018, just 11 years after the programme's revival, UNLV had climbed to 5th place in the national varsity rankings, establishing itself among the leading college debate teams in the US.How did a $1.5 million gift revive UNLV's debate programmeThe university's debate team had a successful history before financial difficulties brought its activities to an end. Budget cuts led to the programme being dismantled in 1998, leaving UNLV without a competitive team for almost a decade.According to the university, the turning point came in 2007 when Dr Sanford and Sandra Berman contributed $1.5 million to revive the programme. Their support helped the university rebuild its team and recruit Jacob Thompson, a communication studies professor who became its coach and director.The donation gave the programme the opportunity to develop again, but establishing a nationally competitive team required more than financial backing. Students needed to develop their research, speaking and debating abilities while building the discipline required to compete against experienced university teams.Thompson's ambition was to create a team capable of winning a national championship while maintaining a strong commitment to teamwork and representing the university responsibly. That approach became an important part of the programme's development.The team established itself among the nation's leading competitorsUNLV's progress became evident within its first few years of returning to competition. In January 2012, the university announced that its Sanford I. Berman Debate Team had entered the top 10 varsity programmes nationally for the first time.According to the university, the team was tied for 10th place with Kansas State University in the National Debate Tournament rankings. It also held the highest ranking in District I, which included universities in California, Arizona and Nevada.The achievement was particularly significant because the programme had existed in its revived form for only 5 years. It demonstrated that UNLV could compete with established institutions and gave the team a stronger position in the national debating community.The university provided another example of that progress. UNLV students Sara Beth Brooks and Matt Gomez won the Las Vegas Classic Invitational Collegiate Debate Tournament, defeating a team from the University of Texas in the final.The competition featured 98 teams from 31 colleges and universities across the western and midwestern United States. Three other UNLV teams also advanced beyond the preliminary rounds into the elimination stage.Intensive preparation helped turn potential into resultsCompetitive policy debating requires participants to understand complicated subjects, construct convincing arguments and respond quickly to opposing views. At UNLV, two-person teams are expected to argue both for and against a proposed policy, giving them experience in examining an issue from different perspectives.Competitors can deliver arguments at approximately 350 to 400 words per minute, considerably faster than an ordinary conversation. The speed allows them to present numerous arguments within the time available, but it also demands extensive preparation.By March 2018, the team's training and competitive experience had produced impressive results. Senior Matthew Gomez and junior Jeffrey Horn won 71 of their 92 debates during the regular season and secured 2 tournament titles.Their performance placed the pair 3rd in the national individual team rankings. UNLV itself stood 5th in the varsity standings, ahead of established competitors including Cornell, Northwestern and Baylor.Gomez and Horn earned automatic qualification for the 2018 National Debate Tournament. Another UNLV pair, senior Roman Kezios and junior Reece Aguilar, qualified after winning the Pacific Champions Debate Tournament in February.A culture of teamwork strengthened the programmeThe university's rise was not built around a single successful partnership. By 2018, the squad consisted of eight 2-person teams, with competitors participating at novice, junior varsity and varsity levels according to their experience.The team's preparation involved substantial time outside regular classes. Gomez and Horn spent approximately 40 to 50 hours each week refining arguments, reviewing evidence and preparing for competition, with their workload increasing before major tournaments.Thompson attributed the programme's improvement to a positive atmosphere, shared effort and the team's growing history of success. The approach also created opportunities for students who had never debated before. Thompson emphasised that undergraduates from different academic backgrounds could join the programme if they were prepared to work hard and develop their abilities.The university explains that alumni have gone on to work in higher education, law, politics and both the public and private sectors. The programme also aims to encourage informed public discussion and improve access to debating opportunities for younger students. Through its summer debate camp, the team mentors middle and high school pupils, helping hundreds of young debaters develop their skills.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ‘Protocol, not power’: Ex-IMF director rebuts Pakistan’s 'historic milestone' claim over 2027 leadership
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former International Monetary Fund (IMF) executive director Krishnamurthy V Subramanian has challenged Pakistan’s claim that its appointment to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former International Monetary Fund (IMF) executive director Krishnamurthy V Subramanian has challenged Pakistan’s claim that its appointment to chair the IMF and World Bank Boards of Governors in 2027 marks a return to global financial leadership, calling the role “protocol, not power”.In a post on X, Subramanian said the chairmanship was ceremonial and rotated annually, arguing that it should not be equated with leadership of a major global economic forum.“Claim: ‘Pakistan is heading back to the top table of global finance after 74 years!’ Reality: Pakistan will chair the IMF-World Bank Annual Plenary in 2027. This chair is purely ceremonial & rotates annually: Paraguay this year, Cabo Verde in 2025. It's protocol, not power,” he wrote.Pakistan was recently named chair of the Boards of Governors of the IMF and the World Bank Group for 2027. The country will take up the position for the first time since 1953, with Pakistan’s Minister for Economic Affairs and World Bank governor, Ahad Khan Cheema, set to assume the role, according to an Islamabad statement.Pakistan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs described the appointment as a “historic milestone”, saying it would give the country an opportunity to contribute to global economic and development discussions and facilitate dialogue among member nations.What Krishnamurthy Subramanian saidIn another post, Subramanian rejected comparisons between India’s presidencies of the G20 and BRICS and Pakistan’s rotating chairmanship of the IMF-World Bank Annual Plenary, calling them a false equivalence.“India's G20 presidency set the agenda for a major forum of global economic cooperation; its BRICS presidency drove an emerging-economies platform... Pakistan's role is to preside over an annual meeting,” he said.Pakistan’s dependence on IMF supportPakistan continues to rely on financial assistance from the IMF through a $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and a $1.4 billion Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).The EFF is intended to address the country’s balance-of-payments needs and support economic reforms, while the RSF provides longer-term financing to help tackle climate-related risks and strengthen economic resilience.Pakistan is also expected to receive around $1.2 billion from the IMF, subject to approval by the fund’s Executive Board. The expected disbursement follows an agreement between IMF staff and Pakistani authorities on the latest reviews of the two loan programmes.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: NBA coach Tyronn Lue turns a former segregated school in his hometown into a community centre as part of his $10 million commitment
articles.summary: In Mexico, Missouri, a former school building has taken on a new role after years away from its original purpose.
articles.body: In Mexico, Missouri, a former school building has taken on a new role after years away from its original purpose. Garfield School, once established to educate Black children during segregation, is now the headquarters of a community initiative founded by Los Angeles Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue. The project brings the historic property back into community use, with education and youth support among its priorities. According to PRNewswire, in July 2025, the building was formally dedicated under a new name honouring Lue's mother and grandmother. The change forms part of a wider $10 million commitment to the town, where Lue grew up and where the school remains part of the area's history.How Garfield School went from a segregated school to a community hubGarfield School was established during the era of racial segregation in the United States, when Black pupils were educated in separate facilities. Its place in Mexico's history extended beyond the classroom, with generations of local families connected to the institution.The school eventually closed and the property was later used by a credit union. Its educational role had ended, leaving a building whose original purpose was tied to a different period in the town's past. Lue's decision to acquire the property created an opportunity to return it to community use, this time through programmes intended to support young people and connect residents with local resources.For Lue, the building also carried a personal connection. He grew up in Mexico, Missouri, and has spoken about the influence of the wider community on his upbringing. The school had been important to local residents, and its closure had been a source of disappointment for people who remembered its earlier role.Tyronn Lue's $10 million commitment to the communityReportedly, the former school is now the base for Commitment to Community (C2C), a $10 million initiative established by Lue. The project is intended to support the Mexico area through educational opportunities, youth programming and partnerships with organisations working in the community.The initiative is being developed in collaboration with the Tyronn Lue Fund and Partners for Rural Impact, a national non-profit organisation focused on expanding educational opportunities in rural communities. The partnership brings together Lue's investment in his hometown and an organisation with experience in supporting young people and families.The school is one part of the broader effort. Buildings next to the property, which had also been acquired from a local credit union, are expected to be adapted for youth activities, resource centres and other community services. These spaces are intended to complement the work based at the former school, giving the initiative room to expand its activities.Kim and Olivia Lue Garfield Legacy Center honours family historyAt a dedication ceremony held in early July 2025, Lue announced that the building would be known as the Kim and Olivia Lue Garfield Legacy Center. The name recognises his mother and grandmother, as well as their connection to Garfield School.The event brought together community members, local leaders and former students. A ribbon-cutting ceremony marked the change, while a community legacy walk and tours of nearby buildings gave attendees an opportunity to see the developing project.The renaming places Lue's family history alongside the school's longer history in Mexico. Rather than being used solely as a headquarters for a charitable initiative, the property is intended to remain connected to the people it serves, with educational programming and local partnerships at the centre of its new role.Tyronn Lue’s C2C initiative looks beyond Garfield School’s dedicationThe July dedication marked an early milestone for C2C, rather than the completion of its work. Plans for the surrounding properties include dedicated areas for youth programmes and community services, while partnerships are expected to help deliver educational opportunities for local families.The initiative also has a fundraising component beyond Missouri. Lue planned to bring attention to the project at the second annual C2C fundraising event for October 19, 2025, at the Intuit Dome in California, the home arena of the Los Angeles Clippers. The event was intended to help support the initiative's wider work.The transformation of Garfield School links the project's future plans with a building that already holds a place in local history. Established to serve Black students during segregation, later used by a credit union and now serving as the home of C2C, the property has passed through several distinct phases. Its latest role centres on education, youth support and community resources in the town where Lue was raised.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1940, a Jewish family's Kandinsky painting was sold under Nazi occupation; 83 years later, their heirs recovered it, and it has now fetched £31.56 million at a London auction after decades of dispute
articles.summary: A painting by Russian artist Wassily Kandinsky, sold under disputed circumstances during Nazi occupation in 1940, has fetched £31.56 million at a London
articles.body: A painting by Russian artist Wassily Kandinsky, sold under disputed circumstances during Nazi occupation in 1940, has fetched £31.56 million at a London auction, bringing renewed attention to one family's decades-long struggle to recover its artwork. The painting, Das bunte Leben (The Colorful Life), was returned to the heirs of its original Jewish owners in 2023, 83 years after the wartime sale. According to auction house Christie's, the 1907 masterpiece became the highest-value lot of its London evening sale on October 14, 2026, following nearly six minutes of competitive bidding.A painting caught in the turmoil of the Second World WarDas bunte Leben was acquired in November 1927 by Hedwig and Emanuel Albert Lewenstein, a Jewish couple who lived in Amsterdam and collected art. The painting was subsequently loaned to the city's Stedelijk Museum in 1933, where it remained on public display. The couple died before the Second World War, leaving their art collection to their two children. Both children left Europe before or during the early stages of the conflict as Nazi Germany's persecution of Jewish people intensified.On October 9, 1940, the Kandinsky painting was sold at an auction in Amsterdam. The sale took place less than five months after German forces occupied the Netherlands. Questions surrounding the circumstances of the transaction later became central to the family's efforts to reclaim the artwork. According to The Times of Israel, the painting was purchased by Salomon Slijper, a Dutch Jewish businessman who survived the war in hiding. The circumstances of the sale remained disputed for decades. Bayerische Landesbank argued that Irma Lewenstein Klein had initiated the auction in connection with a divorce dispute, but the German Advisory Commission found insufficient evidence to establish that she had voluntarily submitted the painting for sale.From private ownership to a German museumThe painting changed hands again in 1972, following Slijper's death. His widow, Johanna, sold it to Bayerische Landesbank, the state bank of Bavaria, for 900,000 Dutch guilders. The bank subsequently lent the artwork to the Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus and Kunstbau museum in Munich, Germany. It remained associated with the institution for approximately five decades, while the Lewenstein family continued to pursue its claim to the painting.In 2017, the family's heirs filed a lawsuit seeking its return. Their claim formed part of the broader effort to recover artworks lost through Nazi persecution, forced sales and other transactions during the Holocaust. Such cases can be difficult to resolve because they involve records of historical ownership, the circumstances in which an artwork changed hands and the legal status of subsequent purchases. In this case, the question was whether the 1940 sale could be considered legitimate given the persecution of Jewish people under Nazi occupation.Restitution after 83 yearsA significant development came in May 2023, when an independent German commission concluded that Das bunte Leben had been lost as a result of the persecution of Jews under German occupation. It recommended that the painting be returned to the Lewenstein heirs. Bayerische Landesbank implemented the recommendation in June 2023, restoring the artwork to the family after decades of uncertainty. The restitution allowed the heirs to regain control of the painting and eventually offer it for sale.The case also illustrates the continuing importance of restitution processes in addressing the legacy of Nazi-looted art. Although the return of an artwork cannot reverse the circumstances in which it was lost, it can acknowledge the injustice suffered by its original owners and their descendants.A record result at Christie's London auctionThe painting's return to the market culminated in its sale at Christie's London auction on October 14, 2026. It achieved £31,560,000, equivalent to approximately $42 million, after almost six minutes of bidding. Christie's reported that the work exceeded its pre-sale estimate of £18 million to £25 million, making it the leading lot of the evening's 20th/21st Century London Evening Sale. The auction house described the painting as an important early work in Kandinsky's artistic development.Painted in 1907, Das bunte Leben depicts a colourful, panoramic scene featuring figures gathered in a landscape, with a walled town crowning a hill in the distance. Its vivid palette and narrative imagery reflect an earlier phase of Kandinsky's career, before his move towards greater abstraction. The sale took place as part of a wider evening of auctions that generated approximately £218.6 million across Christie's combined London sales. According to the auction house, the Kandinsky painting was the highest-value lot of the evening. The identity of the buyer was not disclosed. Beyond its financial value, the painting's journey from a disputed wartime sale to restitution and a multimillion-pound auction underscores how the history of an artwork can remain inseparable from the lives of the people who once owned it.You use AI every day. articles.title: Days after quitting BJP, Bollywood singer Jubin Nautiyal’s father Ramsharan joins Congress
articles.summary: DEHRADUN: Ramsharan Nautiyal, father of Bollywood singer Jubin Nautiyal, joined the Congress on Monday, days after resigning from the Bharatiya Janata
articles.body: DEHRADUN: Ramsharan Nautiyal, father of Bollywood singer Jubin Nautiyal, joined the Congress on Monday, days after resigning from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), marking his return to the party he had left in 2014.Nautiyal’s move comes months ahead of the 2027 Uttarakhand Assembly elections and after he indicated that a lack of respect was behind his decision to leave the BJP.“I have resigned from the Bharatiya Janata Party. If the BJP president has said that the resignation has not been received, that is possible because I did not go personally to submit it. I sent my stenographer to the office,” Nautiyal had said after the resignation row emerged.He later said he had emailed his resignation to the BJP state president, Mahendra Bhatt, after reading reports that the party had not received it.Explaining his decision to quit the BJP, Nautiyal had said that someone who had been associated with an organisation for 10-12 years would not leave without a reason.“But when a person leaves their place, the main reason should be respected. And if respect is not given, then one will distance oneself. That is what I say,” he had said, adding that Bhatt could explain the reasons for his departure.The BJP had earlier said it had not received his resignation, triggering a brief dispute over whether the letter had been formally submitted.(With agency inputs)Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. articles.title: An 18-year-old solved a mathematical problem named after Chicken McNuggets and won €7,000 at a European science contest
articles.summary: An 18-year-old student from Poland has won €7,000 at a European science competition for developing a new method to solve a long-standing mathematical
articles.body: An 18-year-old student from Poland has won €7,000 at a European science competition for developing a new method to solve a long-standing mathematical problem named after McDonald’s Chicken McNuggets. Kazimierz Jakub Chomicz received one of four first prizes at the 2026 European Union Contest for Young Scientists, held at Kiel University in Germany. His research addresses a mathematical puzzle that has challenged researchers for decades, extending the methods available for tackling it to a case involving four different box sizes.How did an 18-year-old approach the Chicken McNugget problemThe problem, formally known as the Chicken McNugget problem, examines which quantities cannot be formed when items are sold in packages of fixed sizes. Although the name comes from chicken nuggets, the underlying mathematics has applications beyond food packaging.According to Kiel University, the puzzle concerns the largest quantity that cannot be obtained by combining packages of specified sizes. Mathematicians call this the Frobenius number, and finding it becomes increasingly difficult as the number of available package sizes increases.For example, if a product is available only in packages containing fixed numbers of items, some quantities may be impossible to make by combining those packages. The challenge is to identify the largest quantity that remains unattainable.The problem has attracted mathematical interest because a straightforward solution is available for 2 package sizes, while the situation becomes considerably more complicated when additional sizes are introduced.Chomicz's research focuses on extending the mathematical approach to 4 package sizes, addressing a part of the problem that has remained difficult to resolve.Why has this mathematical puzzle challenged researchersThe difficulty lies in determining which quantities can be formed from combinations of different package sizes without overlooking any possibilities.Kiel University explains that the Frobenius number can be calculated using a simple formula when there are two package sizes. For three sizes, however, there is no equivalent general formula, although mathematicians have developed a substantial body of results to address the problem.When four or more package sizes are involved, finding solutions becomes even more challenging. Existing approaches have struggled to provide results comparable to those available for the 3-size case.Chomicz's work addresses this gap by introducing a method for solving the problem for any four package sizes. According to the university, the approach directly extends the established results for three sizes and is the first method to achieve a comparable level of strength for four.What did the research achieveThe project, titled Chicken McNugget problem in embedding dimension four, was recognised at the 2026 European Union Contest for Young Scientists, known as EUCYS.In its report on the project, Kiel University described the method as a new approach to a problem that has remained largely out of reach for cases involving four or more package sizes.The research builds on earlier mathematical work rather than treating the problem as an entirely new question. By generalising results already established for three package sizes, it offers a way to address a more complicated version of the same challenge.This distinction matters because mathematical progress often depends on extending an existing result to situations where earlier techniques no longer work effectively. A method that applies to four package sizes provides researchers with a stronger framework for examining the problem.The university's description establishes the scope of the method, although it does not suggest that the broader Chicken McNugget problem has been completely solved for every possible number of package sizes.How did Chomicz win the European science competitionThe award was presented at EUCYS 2026, which brought together young researchers from across Europe and beyond to present projects spanning multiple scientific disciplines.According to Kiel University, 144 participants from 37 countries presented their work to an international panel of experts. The young researchers, aged between 14 and 20, had qualified through national science competitions before reaching the European stage.The competition took place at Kiel University from 22 to 27 September 2026. Participants presented projects they had developed themselves and answered questions from the jury during several rounds of interviews.Chomicz received one of four first prizes, each worth €7,000. The other winning entries covered research into cancer-related biology, medical technology and plant stress detection.What did the other winning projects investigateThe competition recognised projects that approached scientific challenges from very different directions.According to the European Commission's research and innovation department, one first prize went to Georgian researchers Nikoloz Tkebuchava, 17, and Lizi Chachua, 16, for their investigation of the structure and conservation of the FAM163A protein and its potential role in cancer.Canadian researcher Gurnoor Kaur, 17, received another first prize for Eigenpulse, a project aimed at eliminating demographic bias in pulse oximetry and remote photoplethysmography. These technologies are used to measure aspects of the body's physiological condition, making accuracy across different demographic groups an important research objective.The fourth first prize went to Italian teenagers Tommaso Vaninetti, 17, Abdoellah El Makkaoui, 16, and Frida Tirari, 16. Their PlantLeaf project uses a system to detect and analyse how plants react to stress.EUCYS has been organised annually since 1989, bringing together successful participants from national science competitions. The European Commission reported that the 2026 event attracted around 140 young scientists from nearly 40 countries. An international jury of 20 experts assessed the projects, with first, second and third prizes awarded alongside additional special awards.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 1850, a 7-year-old African girl was presented to Queen Victoria as a 'gift'; 176 years later, her great-great-grandson is revisiting her remarkable life through a newly published biography
articles.summary: A seven-year-old African girl who was presented to Queen Victoria as a 'gift' in 1850 went on to become one of the best-known African women in Victorian
articles.body: A seven-year-old African girl who was presented to Queen Victoria as a 'gift' in 1850 went on to become one of the best-known African women in Victorian Britain. But behind her royal connections was a childhood marked by violence, separation from her family, and decisions made largely by others. Now, 176 years later, a newly published biography examines the life of Sarah Forbes Bonetta, while her great-great-grandson, Bayo Randle, reflects on what her experiences meant for his family.The biography, Becoming Sarah Forbes Bonetta: A Yoruba Woman in Queen Victoria’s Court, has been written by Professor Henry Lovejoy of the University of Colorado Boulder. It looks beyond Bonetta's association with the British royal family to examine the circumstances in which she was brought to England, the restrictions placed on her, and the life she eventually built.Randle, a 37-year-old British-Nigerian barrister living in London, discussed his ancestor's story in an interview with The Guardian. During the interview, Randle questioned the idea that a person could be given away as a diplomatic present, while acknowledging that the event had changed the course of his family's history.“I don’t think a human being, who has agency, could be ‘gifted’ from one to another, but had she not been gifted to Queen Victoria, would I be here today?” he asked.A royal upbringing that came with restrictionsFor much of her life, Bonetta was known for her unusual position in British society. Queen Victoria paid for her education, maintained contact with her, and later approved her marriage. She also became godmother to Bonetta's eldest daughter.However, the new biography questions whether this privileged upbringing meant that Bonetta was free to make her own choices.According to Lovejoy's research, British naval captain Frederick Forbes, who brought the girl to England, had requested that she become “the property of the crown”. The historian argues that Bonetta was “effectively indentured to Queen Victoria until age 19”.This finding places her experience in a different light. According to the research, although she received an education and enjoyed connections unavailable to many others, her position was shaped by a system that continued to restrict African people's freedom even after the abolition of slavery.Lovejoy has also examined how more than 700,000 Africans freed from enslavement were subjected to arrangements requiring them to work for years to cover the supposed cost of their freedom and argues that Bonetta occupied a privileged position within this broader system.According to the historian, her achievements were used to support British claims about the benefits of colonial rule in Africa.How Bonetta became part of the royal householdLong before she met Queen Victoria, Bonetta was a child named Aina, born in 1843 in Oke-Odan, in present-day southwest Nigeria.In 1848, forces belonging to King Ghezo of Dahomey attacked her town. Her family was killed, and she was captured at approximately five years old. She remained at the king's court for the next two years.Her circumstances changed when Frederick Forbes, a captain in the Royal Navy's West Africa Squadron, travelled to Dahomey in 1850. He had been sent to persuade King Ghezo to agree to measures against the slave trade.The diplomatic mission did not achieve its intended result, but Forbes returned with the young girl. According to English Heritage, it remains unclear whether Ghezo offered her freely or Forbes negotiated for her release.Before taking her to Britain, Forbes arranged for her baptism and gave her the name Sarah Forbes Bonetta, using his surname and the name of his ship.She met Queen Victoria at Windsor Castle on November 9, 1850. The queen subsequently arranged for her care and education.Bonetta spent time with the Forbes family, attended a missionary school in Sierra Leone and later lived with families in England. Her abilities in languages and music attracted attention, and she became a familiar name in British newspapers.Bonetta's marriage and the life she built in AfricaDespite her close association with the royal family, Bonetta did not spend most of her adult life in England. At 19, she married James Pinson Labulo Davies, a wealthy merchant and philanthropist from Sierra Leone. Their wedding took place on August 14, 1862, with Queen Victoria's approval.But Bonetta had expressed doubts about marrying Davies. In correspondence with Mrs Schoen, whose family had cared for her in England, she questioned whether financial independence was a sufficient reason to accept a marriage.The couple subsequently moved to Africa, living in Sierra Leone and Lagos. They had three children, including their eldest daughter, Victoria, born in 1863 and named after the queen.Bonetta became known for her accomplishments as a linguist, musician, travel writer and educator. Her life in Lagos was an important part of her story, although it has often received less attention than her childhood connection to the British monarchy.Her later years were affected by tuberculosis. She travelled to Madeira, hoping the climate would improve her condition, but died there on August 15, 1880, aged 37.Following her death, Queen Victoria continued to support her daughter Victoria, including helping with her education.Randle wants the full story toldFor Randle, the biography has also brought him closer to parts of his family history that were previously difficult to examine.He first learned about Bonetta from his father, Adekunle Randle, a retired lawyer. His family still possesses an engraved goblet and plate given by Queen Victoria to Bonetta's daughter.One discovery was particularly significant. During his research, Lovejoy located a plaster bust of Bonetta made in 1851 by sculptor Benedetto Pistrucci. Randle subsequently saw the work, which preserves the appearance of his ancestor as a young girl.But the sculpture also reflected the racial attitudes of its time. It had been produced for purposes connected to phrenology, a discredited practice that attempted to draw conclusions about people's characteristics from the shape of their skulls.The biography also disputes several longstanding descriptions of Bonetta, including claims that she was a Yoruba princess and that she herself was Queen Victoria's goddaughter.Randle has welcomed these findings, even when they challenge more familiar versions of his ancestor's life. He believes understanding her experiences requires recognising both the opportunities she received and the control others exercised over her.He also does not want Bonetta to be remembered only for what happened to her as a child. Her education, abilities and achievements in Africa, he believes, deserve attention alongside the circumstances that brought her to Britain.“But it would be a mistake to paint her story as entirely tragic,” he told The Guardian. For Randle, the new biography is an opportunity to understand Bonetta as more than a girl once presented to a queen.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: For some children, summer camp is a few days away from home. For others, it can be the first place where creativity feels like a possibility rather than a privilege. That idea has shaped Camp Firework, an arts-focused summer programme created by Katy Perry and her sister Angela Lerche to give underserved children in California a space to explore, connect and discover their potential.What began in 2019 has now grown into a wider initiative, with nearly 1,000 middle school students attending 12 camps over seven years, states a recent report by KEYT News Channel.A camp built around creativityOrganised through the Firework Foundation, co-founded by Perry and Lerche, Camp Firework brings together children from North and South Santa Barbara County for a three-day residential experience, states the online report.The latest session, held during the summer of 2026, welcomed more than 85 boys and girls between the ages of 10 and 13. The programme blends creative pursuits with outdoor activities, giving campers the chance to experience music, dance, hiking, archery and other experiences away from their everyday surroundings.Rather than focusing solely on traditional classroom learning, the camp places the arts at the centre of personal development. Creativity becomes a way for children to build confidence, form friendships and imagine possibilities beyond their immediate circumstances, adds the report.Reaching children who need it mostAccording to the official website, Camp Firework works with community organisations to identify and refer children who may not otherwise have access to experiences of this kind. articles.title: Around 1910, after more than a decade of work, journalist Charles Lummis completed El Alisal, his hand-built stone home made with Arroyo Seco rocks near Los Angeles
articles.summary: Discover the fascinating story of Charles Lummis, a journalist who took 12 years to build El Alisal, his remarkable hand-crafted stone home in Los Angeles. Learn about the unique construction materials, historical significance, and how it stands as a testament to Lummis' dedication to his craft.
articles.body: Los Angeles has many well-known homes, but most were designed by architects and built by labourers. Charles Fletcher Lummis was a newspaperman who enjoyed physical labor and took an unusual hands-on approach to building his home. He used stones from the Arroyo Seco and worked with Native American laborers, while also consulting architects about structural problems.Charles Fletcher Lummis, the first city editor of the Los Angeles Times, began building El Alisal beside the Arroyo Seco in 1897 and continued working on it until around 1910. The house is mainly formed of riverbed pebbles with mortar, and Lummis did a good deal of the work himself with a few Native American labourers. The same National Register nomination form describes the exterior walls as two to four feet thick and resting on deep concrete footings. How long it took is debatable; estimates vary from 12 to 15 years, and Lummis certainly didn’t do everything completely by himself. Still, the 4,000-square-foot house is real and remains in Highland Park, free to visitors.A walker who wanted a castleLummis (1859-1928) had initially become famous by walking from Cincinnati to Los Angeles in 143 days, sending out letters to newspapers along his route. Later, he became the Times’ first city editor, founded the Southwest Museum and the California Landmarks Club and served as the city’s librarian from 1905 to 1910. In 1895, Lummis chose a three-acre site beside the Arroyo Seco chiefly because of a mammoth, ancient sycamore, according to the California Office of Historic Preservation. That tree gave the house its name, but it has since died and has been replaced by four saplings.Construction started in 1897. Lummis erected a four-room camp house to live in before the main home and planted fruit trees and eucalyptus hedges around the acreage, according to the Homestead Museum's account in a 1900 Harper's Weekly profile. The same source claims that Lummis made the construction job his gymnasium, a balance to the sometimes ten hours a day he spent at his desk.Boulders, railway poles and doors handmadeThe walls are of riverbed boulders in cement, lime and sand mortar; The Society of Architectural Historians in its SAH Archipedia entry also notes that the concrete home is faced with river boulders collected on the site and in the adjacent arroyo. It states the doors and window frames were hand-built and finished using an adze. Recycled Santa Fe Railroad ties and telegraph poles were used in the house’s framing and roof, according to a Los Angeles Times account.The look is Mission Revival with a medieval flair. The front boasts a round turret and an entryway with a door in two sections, each weighing roughly 1,000 pounds, Angelus News reported. The building also expressed, early on, the Arts and Crafts philosophy that a house should be built by hand from local materials.The term “hand-built” does not mean Lummis worked alone. He consulted architects Sumner Hunt and Arthur Benton about structural problems, and historian Jane Apostol later uncovered a 1921 letter in which Hunt described their collaboration. Lummis also received help from Native American labourers. His children later recalled that workers brought from Isleta performed rough labor during construction. Anyway, Lummis was proud of the product, and liked to joke that any fool could write a book, but it required a genuine man to create a dovetail door.A house that withstood a motorwayLummis hosted gatherings he called “noises,” attracting writers, musicians, artists and other notable guests. After Lummis died in 1928, the mansion began to deteriorate. The Arroyo Seco Parkway was built between the house and the arroyo’s flood-control channel in 1940. El Alisal itself nearly faced demolition to make way for the parkway, but it was preserved and is now designated California Historical Landmark No. 531 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places.The mansion served as the headquarters of the Historical Society of Southern California from 1965 until the 2010s and is now run as a museum by the Los Angeles Department of Recreation and Parks. The home is at 200 East Avenue 43 in Los Angeles. Because published listings differ on visiting days and hours, check with the City of Los Angeles Department of Recreation and Parks before making a visit. Lummis wanted a home that reflected the region he spent his life promoting, and he worked on it for more than a decade. The Arroyo Seco Parkway runs just beyond the fence, but El Alisal remains a distinctive stone home built largely by hand.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1908, Henry Mercer began building Fonthill Castle with hand-mixed concrete; the 44-room Pennsylvania home is now a museum
articles.summary: Discover the extraordinary story behind Fonthill, Henry Mercer's hand-made concrete castle in Pennsylvania, featuring 44 rooms, 200 windows, and an impressive collection of tiles. Learn about its unique architecture and how it became a museum over a century later.
articles.body: Reinforced concrete was still an emerging building method in the early 1900s. Archaeologist and tile maker Henry Chapman Mercer of Doylestown, Pennsylvania, saw its potential for an unusual castle that could showcase his collections of tiles and prints. He began building Fonthill in 1908, when he was 51. The project continued through 1912, although the main structure was enclosed by 1910 and finishing work continued afterwards, according to the Society of Architectural Historians. The concrete was mixed by hand by a crew working under Mercer’s direction, while a horse named Lucy helped lift loads to upper levels.An archaeologist with a specific planMercer (1856–1930) was an archaeologist, anthropologist, ceramicist, scholar and antiquarian. He designed Fonthill as both his residence and a showcase for his collections of tiles and prints. The building became an early example of poured reinforced concrete, allowing Mercer to shape the structure around the rooms he planned.The crew was small. Eight, sometimes ten, labourers who had never worked with concrete were hired under Mercer’s constant direction and learned his pouring methods as they went. The trade magazine Concrete Decor reports that no machinery was used, and that even the water was pumped by hand. A plaster of Paris model and his sketches stood in for blueprints. The museum adds that a horse named Lucy hoisted loads of mixed concrete up to the workers.Rooms, tiles and unexpected luxuriesMercer planned Fonthill from the inside out, developing its rooms before shaping the exterior. The castle combines mediaeval, Gothic and Byzantine influences. Its 44 rooms include 10 bathrooms, five bedrooms and 18 fireplaces, while its more than 200 windows vary in size and design. The unusual layout reflects Mercer’s interest in creating a house that did not follow conventional architectural plans.Tiles cover many of Fonthill’s walls and ceilings. Mercer incorporated his own Arts and Crafts designs alongside tiles from Persia, China, Spain and Holland. For some decorated ceilings, workers arranged tiles upside down in a graded layer of sand before pouring concrete over them. Once the concrete had cured and the supports were removed, the tiled surfaces were exposed. Despite its medieval appearance, the house included modern conveniences such as two dumbwaiters, an Otis elevator, an intercom buzzer system and telephones for communication between rooms. The museum documents this method in its construction history.Visiting Fonthill todayMercer died in 1930 and left Fonthill in trust to become a museum of decorative tiles and prints. Fonthill is open Tuesday to Sunday, 10 am to 5 pm and can only be seen on a 60-minute guided tour according to the museum’s ticket page. Adult tickets are $20, and the museum suggests booking beforehand as last-minute tickets are not guaranteed. It also warns of steep steps and tiny, uneven tunnels and does not suggest it for anyone with restricted mobility or a fear of small spaces. The Mercer Museum requires a separate ticket; hours may vary, so check before you go. Fonthill remains a striking example of Mercer’s experimental approach to architecture, combining hand-mixed concrete, intricate tilework and an unconventional layout. More than a century later, its unusual rooms and varied windows continue to distinguish it from conventional homes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: LUCKNOW: In a major push towards women’s safety and justice, Lakhimpur Kheri police secured convictions in more than 50 cases involving crimes against
articles.body: LUCKNOW: In a major push towards women’s safety and justice, Lakhimpur Kheri police secured convictions in more than 50 cases involving crimes against women and girls in 2026, while tracing and reuniting 1,145 missing and abducted women and girls with their families under the Uttar Pradesh government’s Mission Shakti 6.0 campaign and Operation Conviction.According to district police data, courts decided 33 rape and POCSO cases this year, resulting in convictions in 23 cases and the sentencing of more than 34 accused. Police also secured convictions in 13 of the 15 dowry death cases decided during the period. Significantly, all seven molestation cases adjudicated by courts this year ended in convictions, giving the district a 100% conviction rate in that category.Several convictions resulted in severe punishments. Multiple accused in rape and gang rape cases involving minor girls were sentenced to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment, while several accused in dowry death and murder cases received life imprisonment along with fines.Among the cases highlighted by police were long-pending rape, POCSO and dowry death cases that ended in convictions following coordinated investigations and prosecution. Officials said sustained monitoring of serious cases and close coordination between investigators and prosecutors played a key role in securing convictions.Alongside these courtroom successes, police carried out an extensive district-wide drive to trace missing women and girls. Under Mission Shakti 6.0, police traced and reunited 1,145 women and girls with their families. articles.title: In 1976, Minnesota rebuilt a four-lane highway using 50% recycled asphalt; when engineers examined it 15 years later, its lifespan matched ordinary pavement
articles.summary: Discover how Minnesota's 1976 highway project utilizing 50% recycled asphalt proved to match the lifespan of conventional pavement after 15 years, demonstrating the viability of asphalt recycling in road construction.
articles.body: Minnesota used recycled asphalt that contained 50% reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) to reconstruct a four-lane urban highway in 1976, and engineers examined pavement cores and visually inspected the road fifteen years later, before a planned milling and overlay project. The project was built in Maplewood, Minnesota, and was among the early US efforts that tested whether old road material could be reused in new pavement without compromising its performance.A four-lane highway became a recycling testIn the 1976 project, the original pavement had to be removed and the road had to be rebuilt with recycled hot-mix asphalt. The new pavement structure included a 175-millimetre (6.9-inch) recycled asphalt base, a 40-mm (1.6-inch) binder course and a 20-mm (0.75-inch) surface wearing course. The recycled asphalt mixture contained 50% RAP, which came from existing asphalt pavement that had been removed and incorporated into the new mix. Engineers reused the old material in the reconstructed pavement rather than sending it to disposal. The project also included a control section built with conventional hot-mix asphalt, and that comparison allowed engineers to assess the recycled pavement against a road section that was made with the help of standard materials.Workers placed the recycled base on the eastbound roadway in three layers, while the westbound base went down in a single layer, and engineers could therefore examine differences in pavement response as well as compare recycled and conventional asphalt. The FHWA's technical account records the project as Minnesota's first recycled hot-mix asphalt installation, and its findings were later included in the agency's review of performance data from early recycling projects across several states.Engineers examined the road after 15 yearsThe first structural measurements came in 1977, after one year of service, and engineers used a Benkelman beam to measure pavement deflection under load, which is a test that helps in assessing how a pavement structure responds to traffic. The measurements showed similar deflection values for the recycled and conventional asphalt sections, which could be analysed as evidence that the two pavement structures had comparable structural strength.But the difference between the recycled sections was that the base that was placed in one layer had a higher average deflection than the base installed in three layers, and the early measurements therefore indicated that construction technique could affect how the pavement responded even when the material contained the same proportion of reclaimed asphalt. The longer-term assessment took place in 1991, when the pavement sections were examined before a milling and overlay project.The inspection found that the recycled mixture had a service life that could be compared to the conventional hot-mix asphalt control section, and the finding covered the 15-year period between the original construction and the 1991 evaluation. The result documented the performance of a specific pavement project that used a particular mix design and construction method.Reusing old asphalt became standard roadworkContractors can mill or remove existing pavement, process the material and blend it into new hot-mix asphalt, which shows how reclaimed asphalt pavement is now widely used in asphalt production. The FHWA explains that recycled asphalt mixtures can perform comparably to conventional pavement when they are properly designed and produced, and also notes that the appropriate RAP content depends on mixture design, material properties and project requirements.Minnesota's early project provided a long-term comparison between recycled and conventional pavement under actual road conditions, and the 1991 inspection found no service-life disadvantage for the recycled mixture in that test section. The experiment also distinguished between the percentage of reclaimed material in the asphalt mix and the performance of the finished road, since a mixture that contained 50% RAP still required appropriate layer thicknesses, construction methods and engineering evaluation. The Maplewood project began in 1976, when asphalt recycling was still being tested, and by the time engineers examined the pavement in 1991, it had completed 15 years of service.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2005, scientists used dye to follow water disappearing beneath Yellowstone; it traveled 1.45 miles underground and reached a spring in less than 24 hours
articles.summary: In 2005, researchers used fluorescent dye to track groundwater movement in Yellowstone National Park, discovering rapid flow beneath Sylvan Pass to Mammoth Crystal Springs. The study revealed insights into aquifer permeability and surface water interactions.
articles.body: Scientists used fluorescent dye to study the groundwater in Yellowstone National Park in June 2005, and found that water that was disappearing into loose rock deposits travelled southeast through the underground system before emerging at Mammoth Hot Springs. The U.S. Geological Survey reported that groundwater covered a distance of 1.45 miles and had a vertical drop of about 500 feet in less than one day. The findings were documented by USGS hydrologists Lawrence E. Spangler and David D. Susong, who found a rapid underground connection between the area where stream water disappeared and the spring where it re-emerged.Scientists followed water beneath Sylvan PassThe investigation took place in the Sylvan Pass area of Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming, and researchers wanted to establish how surface water contributed to groundwater flow reaching Mammoth Crystal Springs. During the June 2005 field investigation, scientists used dye tracing to follow water that disappeared into talus deposits, which consist of loose rock fragments accumulated on slopes. The dye was used to track the water's movement through the subsurface, and researchers detected the tracer at Mammoth Crystal Springs, which established a connection between the area where the stream lost water and the spring farther away.The USGS report estimated that groundwater travelled 1.45 miles and descended about 500 feet before reaching the springs in less than a day, and based on those measurements, the researchers calculated apparent groundwater movement of at least 8,000 feet per day. The speed could be compared to movement that was observed in karst aquifers, where groundwater can travel quickly through interconnected openings, fractures and channels in soluble rock. The report, however, focused on the specific geological conditions at Sylvan Pass rather than suggesting that all Yellowstone groundwater follows the same route.The dye revealed two different travel timesGroundwater travel time to the springs was less than one day, but the researchers recorded peak dye concentrations approximately two days after injection, while the transit of most of the dye mass through the underground system took about three weeks. These measurements describe different stages of the tracer's movement, with the first indicating how quickly groundwater could reach the springs, while the later measurements describe how the concentration of dye changed over time as the tracer moved through the aquifer.The researchers also examined the relationship between groundwater flow and changes in spring discharge, and found that spring flow varied considerably as a response to snowmelt runoff and precipitation. The water that emerged at the spring-fed lake contained high concentrations of suspended sediment, which increased its turbidity, and the report identified these observations as further evidence of the aquifer's high permeability and rapid response to changing water conditions.What the test established about Yellowstone's groundwaterIt was established that water that disappeared into the rock deposits at Sylvan Pass was not simply lost from the local surface-water system, and at least part of it travelled underground towards Mammoth Crystal Springs. The results also documented how quickly that groundwater could move, since a journey of 1.45 miles in less than a day indicated a highly permeable underground pathway between the two locations.The USGS report linked the rapid movement to the aquifer's physical characteristics, with its findings being specific to the Sylvan Pass area and the groundwater system that was examined by the researchers. The work formed part of a larger effort to understand the relationship between surface water and groundwater in Yellowstone National Park, and such connections matter when scientists assess where water travels after it disappears from streams, how springs respond to weather and snowmelt, and how groundwater contributes to surface-water systems. The 2005 dye test supplied a direct measurement of that connection at Sylvan Pass, and documented both the rapid arrival of groundwater at Mammoth Crystal Springs and the longer period that was required for most of the injected dye to pass through the system.You use AI every day. articles.title: Shaquille O’Neal’s $24 million Las Vegas youth complex nears completion; 87,000-square-foot centre will feature sports and education facilities
articles.summary: The Shaquille O’Neal Youth Complex is a $24 million development planned for Las Vegas, bringing together youth programmes, educational support and sports
articles.body: The Shaquille O’Neal Youth Complex is a $24 million development planned for Las Vegas, bringing together youth programmes, educational support and sports facilities. According to FOX5 Las Vegas, the 87,000-square-foot complex is being developed by The Shaquille O’Neal Foundation in partnership with Boys & Girls Clubs of Southern Nevada and Communities In Schools of Southern Nevada. The project is expected to be completed in late 2026, with the complex scheduled to open in early 2027, according to FOX5 Las Vegas. The development is intended to bring sports, education and support services together at one site in northeast Las Vegas, an area that a local nonprofit leader has described as a “service desert”.Shaquille O’Neal Youth Complex: sports facilities and youth services planned for Las VegasThe complex is designed around several spaces serving different needs. According to The Shaquille O’Neal Foundation, the project includes a 30,000-square-foot Boys & Girls Clubs of Southern Nevada clubhouse and what the foundation describes as the country’s first Communities In Schools Alumni Center. The alumni centre is intended to support former Communities In Schools students, with backing from the Elaine P. Wynn & Family Foundation. The planned facilities also include a multi-sports field sponsored by the Las Vegas Raiders and a UFC-themed mixed martial arts and boxing centre. FOX5 Las Vegas has also reported plans for a Lakers-themed gymnasium and basketball court, supported by the Los Angeles Lakers.Inside the clubhouse, planned amenities include an early childhood learning centre, a gymnasium, mental wellness rooms and technology and innovation labs. The foundation describes the planned resources as serving young people from pre-kindergarten through grade 12, with academic, social, emotional, recreational and technology support. The foundation’s Las Vegas facility page says the Boys & Girls Club facility is expected to serve between 150 and 180 young people after school each day. The project was designed by Carpenter Sellers Del Gatto, with CORE Construction serving as the builder. These facilities form part of the wider 87,000-square-foot development, combining youth programming, education and sports on a single site.Shaquille O’Neal Youth Complex timeline: county land donation and June 2025 groundbreakingThe project progressed from a county land donation to a groundbreaking ceremony in June 2025. Clark County commissioners approved the donation of a 5-acre site to The Shaquille O’Neal Foundation in July 2024, according to the foundation and local reporting. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on June 27, 2025, bringing together representatives of the foundation, local youth organisations and sports partners. According to KLAS 8 News Now, the site is near the intersection of Lamb and Lake Mead boulevards in northeast Las Vegas. Andy Bischel of Boys & Girls Clubs of Southern Nevada described the area as a “service desert”, highlighting the need for additional youth resources.O’Neal, who has lived in Las Vegas for decades, said the world would be a better place if every prominent person took care of the community where they lived. Speakers at the groundbreaking included Dr. Lisa Morris Hibbler of the foundation, Las Vegas Raiders president Sandra Douglass Morgan and Tami Hance-Lehr of Communities In Schools of Nevada. In an April 2026 report, FOX5 Las Vegas said construction had reached its halfway point. The report also covered O’Neal’s visit to the site with UFC president Dana White and Raiders owner Mark Davis. This describes the project’s reported status at that time, rather than confirming its current construction progress. The Youth Sports Business Report also reported that O’Neal’s eldest daughter, Taahirah, joined the foundation’s board in connection with the project. The development brings together county land, the foundation’s development efforts and support from sports organisations and youth-service partners.Why the Shaquille O’Neal Youth Complex matters: youth services and what happens nextThe complex is intended to expand access to after-school activities, educational resources and youth support services in northeast Las Vegas. The foundation says the Boys & Girls Club will provide academic, social, emotional and technology support, while the Communities In Schools Alumni Center is intended to help former students with their personal, academic and professional development. KLAS reported that Tami Hance-Lehr described the alumni centre as a development that would be a game-changer and said its team would help young graduates with job placement. The project also reflects O’Neal’s own connection to youth programmes. The Shaquille O’Neal Foundation identifies him as a member of the Boys & Girls Club Alumni Hall of Fame. The Youth Sports Business Report has also noted that he developed his basketball skills at Boys & Girls Club facilities.The project has expanded considerably from its earlier plans. The Las Vegas Review-Journal reported in July 2024 that the proposed facility was expected to cost $16 million and cover 17,000 square feet. The current development is planned to span 87,000 square feet and includes additional sports facilities associated with the Las Vegas Raiders, UFC and the Los Angeles Lakers. The current $24 million project therefore reflects a substantially larger development than the one described in the earlier report. The foundation has also invited prospective donors to enquire about naming opportunities for rooms and other spaces in the complex. Interested parties can contact the foundation for further details. The project is expected to be completed in late 2026, with opening planned for early 2027. Families seeking information about programme schedules, registration and access should look for announcements from the foundation and its local partners as the opening approaches. The development brings together public land, philanthropic support and partnerships with sports organisations and youth-service providers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Israel arrests 10 suspects over attacks on journalist, European diplomats in West Bank
articles.summary: Israeli police have arrested at least 10 suspects over attacks by Israeli settlers on Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine and a group of European
articles.body: Israeli police have arrested at least 10 suspects over attacks by Israeli settlers on Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine and a group of European diplomats in the occupied West Bank, amid growing US pressure on Israel to curb settler violence.The arrests were made under an operation named “Olive Leaf”, launched in coordination with the Israeli military, police said. Security forces searched the areas where the attacks took place, seized vehicles and collected evidence linking the suspects to the incidents, CNN reported.“We are working to collect evidence, findings and testimonies and to consolidate an evidentiary infrastructure that will enable bringing those involved to justice,” Israeli police superintendent Moshe Pinchi said in a statement.US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee welcomed the arrests, describing them as a “very positive development” in efforts to identify and punish those responsible for assaulting Levine.Two attacks during olive harvestLevine, a veteran photojournalist, was assaulted on Friday while travelling with a group of Palestinians at the start of the olive harvest in the Binyamin region.She was hospitalised and underwent surgery on Saturday, with reports describing her condition as moderate.A day later, settlers attacked a group of European diplomats visiting Taybeh, a Palestinian Christian town east of Ramallah.The incident drew condemnation from European governments and Canada, with officials calling for accountability and better protection for civilians and diplomatic representatives.Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar condemned the violence and said a police investigation had been opened. He also noted that the diplomatic delegation’s visit had not been coordinated with the Israeli military in advance.The Israeli military separately condemned the attack and said soldiers had accompanied police and forensic investigators to collect evidence and record witness testimony.A preliminary military inquiry found that no Israeli soldiers were present when the attack occurred.US urges Israel to curb settler violenceThe arrests came after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the Trump administration had urged Israel to take action against settler violence in the West Bank.“We’ve asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff,” Rubio said on Saturday, according to CNN. He added that President Donald Trump did not want to see tensions escalate into a crisis in the territory.Israeli human rights group Yesh Din has documented more than 530 incidents of settler violence since the olive harvest began in late September, averaging 27 incidents a day.Israeli soldiers were present during roughly a quarter of the attacks documented over the period, the group said.Despite video footage of the assaults on Levine and the diplomats, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has questioned aspects of the incidents, saying “serious questions remain”.He has repeatedly described settler violence as the actions of a rogue group, a position that has drawn scrutiny amid concerns over the scale of the attacks.Separately, Israel’s defence minister said on Monday that he would not reinstate administrative detention for Jewish Israelis, a measure that allows suspects to be held without charge or trial. articles.title: Polish PM Donald Tusk to visit India from October 21 to 23, hold talks with PM Modi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk will visit India from October 21 to 23 at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with the two
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk will visit India from October 21 to 23 at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with the two leaders set to review bilateral ties and discuss regional and global issues of mutual interest, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Monday.Tusk will be accompanied by Andrzej Domański, Poland's minister of finance and economy, along with a large business delegation, according to an official statement issued by the government.During the visit, Tusk will hold bilateral talks with PM Modi in New Delhi on October 22. The discussions will cover the full range of India-Poland relations, which were elevated to a Strategic Partnership during PM Modi's visit to Poland in August 2024.The two leaders will also exchange views on regional and global developments of mutual interest, the MEA said.Business forums planned in Delhi and BengaluruTusk will also travel to Bengaluru, where he is scheduled to meet business stakeholders, including representatives from the information technology and space sectors.An India-Poland Business Forum will be held in New Delhi on October 22 and in Bengaluru on October 23.The visit is expected to advance cooperation across several areas, including trade and investment, defence, emerging technologies, renewable energy, education, culture and people-to-people ties."The visit will provide the opportunity to further strengthen the India-Poland Strategic Partnership and advance cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, defence, emerging technologies, renewable energy, education, culture and people-to-people ties," the MEA said in its statement.The visit will also provide an opportunity to deepen the strategic partnership between India and the European Union, it added.Second India visit as Polish prime ministerThis will be Tusk's second visit to India in his capacity as Poland's prime minister. His first visit in the role took place in 2010, during his earlier tenure. He also visited New Delhi in 2017 for the India-EU Summit as president of the European Council.The upcoming visit follows the elevation of India-Poland relations to a Strategic Partnership in August 2024, when PM Modi travelled to Warsaw. The visit marked the first trip by an Indian prime minister to Poland in 45 years.During that visit, the two countries adopted a comprehensive five-year action plan covering areas such as trade and investment, defence, energy, green technologies, agriculture and infrastructure.Defence and industrial cooperation on agendaAhead of Tusk's visit, Polish finance and economy minister Andrzej Domański outlined plans to expand trade and defence cooperation with India.Speaking to news agency ANI on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, earlier this month, Domański said Poland wanted to strengthen industrial partnerships and increase defence exports to India."We want to develop a strong defence industry. To do this, we would certainly like to maintain good trade relations in defence products with trusted partners like India. Therefore, it is no surprise that we would also like to increase the export of our defence products to India. During the visit, we will bring Polish defence companies to India," Domański said.The minister's remarks came after his meeting with Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal.The upcoming visit will provide an opportunity for the two countries to discuss cooperation in defence and other strategic sectors alongside their existing economic and diplomatic engagement.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Rwandan dissident, former army officer, found beheaded in Uganda
articles.summary: A Rwandan dissident and former army officer was found beheaded in neighbouring Uganda, police said on Monday.
articles.body: A Rwandan dissident and former army officer was found beheaded in neighbouring Uganda, police said on Monday.The remains of Sergeant Major Robert Kabera, who served in the Rwandan army before fleeing to Uganda in 2020, were discovered on Saturday in a bush in the Kamengo area of Mpigi district, outside the capital, Kampala, Superintendent of Police Lydia Tumushabe told The Associated Press.“The head, up to now, is still missing. Kabera’s body was identified by residents as well as his brother,” Tumushabe said, adding that detectives had yet to establish a clear motive for the killing.According to Uganda’s National Police spokesperson, Rusoke Kituuma, Kabera’s previous service in the Rwandan military had been brought to the attention of investigators.“There are those who allege that he was previously a serving soldier,” Kituuma told reporters. “Whatever. All that we shall establish in the course of investigations.”Who was Robert KaberaAs a soldier, Kabera was a well-known figure in Rwanda, and performed with the Army Jazz Band, according to a 2008 profile published by the local newspaper The New Times.After he fled to Uganda, the Rwandan military launched an investigation into allegations that he had engaged in “unlawful sexual contact” with a family member. Kabera told some Ugandan media outlets that he had fled Rwanda to escape "persecution."His YouTube channel, Major Robert TV, had more than 140,000 followers and featured over 800 videos. His commentary was viewed by some Rwandans as damaging to the image of the Rwandan government.Rwandan authorities had not immediately commented on Kabera’s death.Spotlight on Rwandan President Paul KagameRwanda’s government denies targeting political opponents, despite allegations from critics of President Paul Kagame that his “authoritarian stance” leaves little room for dissent. Several senior military officers have fallen out with Kagame, with some fleeing into exile over fears for their lives, while others have died in prison.Kagame is credited with rebuilding Rwanda after the devastation of the 1994 genocide. However, his government continues to face criticism from human rights groups over alleged widespread abuses, restrictions on independent media and the suppression of political opposition.
